_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.trinity.jack` is a semio-NATIVE assembly scene: a labelled property graph whose edges address PORTS over a kind manifest. No graph library models a port-addressed endpoint and none reads `.dsl.semio`, so the reference is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION in Python written from this subset's committed snapshot schema, mutation grammar and specification vectors.

oracles.rationale: A second implementation of the `s.trinity.jack` parent document, of its `.dsl.semio` carrier and of its one parent-lane mutation `set-query`, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/🔌️mutate-jack-1/🐍️.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` and `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio`; it imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. The scene (nodes with ports, edges over `node@port` endpoints) lives in the composed `content` child (`s.stdio.semio@v1/graph`, design §20.15): its edits are that shared graph vocabulary's leaves and are adjudicated by the graph subset's own oracles, not here. A third-party library was declined: no graph library reads this carrier or models the document's query member. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

candidatesConsidered.reason: `networkx`, `igraph` and `petgraph` model vertices and edges but have no notion of a PORT-addressed endpoint, of a manifest that closes the kind vocabulary, or of the untyped property bag `change-data-property` and `remove-data-property` edit, and none of them reads this carrier.
